long_biography.plain_text:
Automated traffic enforcement shaped John T. Petrozza's career from the 1990s, when he represented Mulvihill Electric in early red-light-camera programmes. As a senior officer of the Staten Island contractor, he founded its Intelligent Control Systems division to build and operate camera-based traffic infrastructure. His work developed within a family-business setting: his wife, Hollis Mulvihill Petrozza, was a vice-president of the family-owned company.

After the division became part of American Traffic Solutions, Petrozza oversaw construction, engineering and field operations across the Americas. His remit covered municipal camera deployments, New York operations and national field-service teams. He also served as an executive officer, director and promoter of ATS Consolidated and held an ownership interest in the wider business. New York records later listed him as an owner of Mulvihill ICS.
